question.:question/problem: Consider the plane curve $4 x^{2} + y^{2}=8.$  Find the equation of the normal line to the curve at the point $(-1,2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If we set $f(x,y)=4 x^{2} + y^{2}$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=8.$  

A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(-1,2)$ can be found by computing $∇f(-1,2).$ 

So, we find the gradient and evaluate it at $(-1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4 x^{2} + y^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(4 x^{2} + y^{2})\,j \\  & =(8 x)\,i+(2 y)\,j \\ ∇f(-1,2) & =(8 (-1))\,i+(2 (2))\,j \\  & =(-8)\,i+(4)\,j \\  & =⟨-8,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $∇f(-1,2)=⟨-8,4⟩$ is a normal vector to the curve at $(-1,2).$

Finally, the Cartesian equation of the line that is parallel to $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y}⟩$ and passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}} & =\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}} \\ \frac{x-(-1)}{-8} & =\frac{y-(2)}{4} \\ (4)(x-(-1)) & =(-8)(y-(2)) \\ (1)(x-(-1)) & =(-2)(y-(2)) \\ x + 1 & =4 - 2 y \\ x + 2 y - 3 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
